routes.label: List the powers and match the shared digit

question:
Three-digit powers of \(2\) and \(5\) are used in this “cross-number” puzzle. What is the only possible digit for the outlined square? \[\begin{array}{lcl} \textbf{\text{ACROSS}} & & \textbf{\text{DOWN}} \\ \textbf{2. } 2^m & & \textbf{1. } 5^n \end{array}\]

[Figure 1](figures/2000_AMC_8_Q09_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The shared square connects the two clues: it is the middle digit of the downward entry and the first digit of the across entry. Listing the three-digit powers lets us use this connection.

For powers of \(5\),
\[
5^2=25,\quad 5^3=125,\quad 5^4=625,\quad 5^5=3125.
\]
Successive powers increase, so the only three-digit possibilities are \(125\) and \(625\). Both have tens digit \(2\). Therefore the across entry must begin with \(2\).

For powers of \(2\),
\[
2^6=64,\quad 2^7=128,\quad 2^8=256,
\]
\[
2^9=512,\quad 2^{10}=1024.
\]
Thus the complete list of three-digit possibilities is \(128,256,512\). Only \(256\) begins with \(2\), and it works with either downward entry. The outlined square is its units digit, so it contains \(\boxed{6}\), choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
